summary: The walk's gone-code rule in .taad/fitness.yaml now catches `case 2 or 3:`, `case (2 or 3):`, `case 3 or 2:` and the switch-expression arm spellings (`2 or 3 =>`, `2 => ..., 3 => ...`). The old `case` pattern is replaced and a switch-arm pattern is added. Both patterns are quiet on Scanner.cs under .NET and under Python `re`, which the Fitness gate uses. I added the two engine tests verbatim, 33 new corpus rows (22 fire, 11 quiet) and a sweep test that holds `Scanner.FolderVanished` to `SizeProbe.IsGone` for every code 0..2000. Against the old rule the two new tests and the new fire rows failed; with the fix the two engine commands pass (3 of 3, 5 of 5), and the full suite passes (1389 of 1389).

files.why: walk rule: `\bcase\s+[23]\s*:` replaced by a case pattern that takes `(`, `or` chains and other codes beside the 2 or 3; a switch-arm pattern added; `because` extended with the new spellings
33 rows added (22 fire, 11 quiet) for case and switch-arm combinator spellings; `about` updated with what the class covers and what it does not
new fact TheWalksPredicateAgreesWithSizeProbeIsGoneForEveryCode: FolderVanished(code,false)==SizeProbe.IsGone(code) for 0..2000, and never true when opened (lesson #903)

mandatory.where: .taad/fitness.yaml walk rule (new `case` pattern and arm pattern); tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/SL005ReviewGoneCodeCaseSpellingTests.cs passes 3 of 3; corpus rows w-case-or, w-case-paren-or, w-switch-arm-or

.taad/fitness.yaml walk rule; tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/GoneCodePatternCombinatorSpellingTests.cs passes 5 of 5; corpus rows w-case-or-reversed, w-case-paren-or-bare, w-switch-arm-or-plain, w-switch-arm-each

obligations.how: SC-080's fix is built and its engine test passes. The class is closed in a corpus: GoneCodeSpellingsCorpus.json holds 33 new rows (22 fire, 11 quiet). The fire rows cover `case`, `case (…)`, `or` chains in either order or with another code or constant beside them, and switch arms, lone, each-arm, own-line and with `when`. The quiet rows cover `case 23`, `case 32 or 20`, denied/87 chains, the 'without case (ContainerLayerStore)' comment, `=> 2` and `n => n + 2`. Before the fix the new fire rows and the test failed; after it they pass. The corpus's own 'about' states the bound: spellings produced by ordinary code, not relational patterns, hex or variables.

SC-081's fix is built and its engine test passes (5 of 5). It uses the same corpus and the same rule change. The switch-arm pattern is the one that also fires on `{ 2 => true, 3 => true }`, and the corpus has that as w-switch-arm-each. The 'show it failing before the fix' evidence is the run against the unfixed rule: 3 of 3 combinator rows in the SC-080 test and 5 of 5 in the SC-081 test failed, plus the new corpus fire rows.

deviations: SC-080 prescribes the arm pattern `\b[23]\s+or\s+[23]\s*=>` and SC-081 prescribes `\b[23]\s*(?:or\s+[23]\s*)?=>`. I built neither verbatim. SC-080's does not fire on SC-081's required `{ 2 => true, 3 => true }` row, and SC-081's misses `2 or 3 or 5 =>`, `5 or 2 or 3 =>` and `(2 or 3) =>`. The built arm pattern is `\b(?:[\w.]+\s+or\s+)*[23]\b(?:\s+or\s+[\w.]+)*\s*\)*(?:\s+when\b[^=\r\n]*)?\s*=>`, a superset of both.

The `case` pattern is also wider than prescribed: `\bcase\s+(?:\(?\s*[\w.]+\s+or\s+)*\(?\s*[23]\b` also catches `case 5 or 3:` and `case Kernel32.X or 3:`, not only a 2 or 3 first. It still leaves `case 23:` quiet. I did this because the batch asks for the class to be closed, and the wider form is quiet on Scanner.cs and on the quiet corpus rows.

Added a behavioural sweep test (FolderVanished vs SizeProbe.IsGone for 0..2000) that neither row asked for, because lesson #903 names it as the closure for predicate drift that no text rule can hold. It changes no src.
not_built: Relational patterns (`>= 2 and <= 3`), a code held in a variable or in hex, and a gone predicate that never spells a number are not caught by the text rule. The corpus `about` says so, and the sweep test covers drift inside the predicate itself.
No per-file census of where the gone codes may appear in Scanner.cs (lesson #43). The text rule stays a tripwire for named spellings and the sweep carries the behaviour.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SL005ReviewGoneCodeCaseSpellingTests|FullyQualifiedName~GoneCodePatternCombinatorSpellingTests|FullyQualifiedName~VanishedFolderCorpusTests" (before the rule change)
tests.note: Expected failure with the old rule: 3 of 3 SC-080 theory rows, 5 of 5 SC-081 theory rows, and the new corpus fire rows failed. This is the code-before-fix evidence.
One of 130 failed: my own row w-switch-arm-when (`2 when !opened => true,`) was not caught by the first arm pattern. I added an optional `when` clause to the pattern; the full run then passed.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 test FsAnalyser.slnx -- xUnit.MaxParallelThreads=2
tests.note: Whole suite, exit 0: 1389 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. It includes TheRulesAreQuietOnTheSourcesTheyGuard, the new sweep test and the rules-parity check.

tests.command: python -I (reads .taad/fitness.yaml, runs the walk rule's four patterns with Python re over the whole of src/FsAnalyser.Core/Scanning/Scanner.cs)
tests.note: Run the way the Fitness gate runs it. All four patterns are quiet on Scanner.cs, comments included.

follow_ups: The two SL-005 review test files each carry their own copy of the yaml pattern reader that VanishedFolderCorpusTests.PatternsOf already has. The engine requires them verbatim, so they were left; they could share one reader later.
